observations: Three pointers 0aac, 0aba and 0ac8 address consecutive 14-byte regions before the target UCASE table.
The first two are passed to the same routine; the third is passed to a nearby related routine.
The shared routine accesses fields at offsets 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 0a and 0c and exchanges several fields with existing DOS data.
Nearby directory processing masks the directory attribute with 0fh and compares the result with 0fh.
The 42 bytes account for the target UCASE table displacement relative to the historical source, with the following historical swap-end padding byte retained in the layout.
limitations: The boundaries are supported by repeated pointers and field access, but original structure names and individual field semantics are not established.
The long-filename association is suggested by the directory attribute handling and needs full caller reconstruction.
There may be additional layout changes elsewhere that happen to cancel; complete linkage is not proven.
